source_batch.unit_label: BFM Module D unit 1 (courseware unit 26): components of assets and liabilities in the bank balance sheet and their management

facts.statement: Balance sheet forms and structure (courseware): under section 29 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 commercial banks prepare a balance sheet and profit and loss account as on the last working day of the year in the forms in the Third Schedule, as specified by the Government in consultation with the central bank. A bank balance sheet comprises sources of funds (capital, reserves, deposits, borrowings, other liabilities and provisions) and applications of funds (cash in hand and balances with the central bank, balances with banks and money at call and short notice, investments, advances, fixed assets, other assets). Liabilities and net worth are the sources; assets are the uses of funds that generate revenue for the bank.

Components of liabilities (courseware): capital is the owners stake and a cushion for depositors and creditors to fall back on in case of losses, a long-term source; the minimum capital requirement is set by the central bank through the capital adequacy ratio. Reserves and surplus include statutory reserves, capital reserves, share premium, revenue and other reserves and the balance in profit and loss account. Deposits are the main source of funds: demand deposits (current deposits, overdue deposits, call deposits), savings bank deposits and term deposits (fixed, short, recurring) repayable after a specified period. Borrowings are borrowings and refinance from the central bank, other commercial banks and institutions such as IDBI, EXIM Bank and NABARD. Other liabilities and provisions: bills payable (drafts, telegraphic transfers, travellers cheques, mail transfers, pay slips, bankers cheques), the net credit balance of inter-office adjustments, interest accrued but not due on deposits and borrowings, and others (provisions for income tax, tax deducted at source, other provisions).

Components of assets (courseware): cash and balances with the central bank include cash in hand (including foreign currency notes and cash in overseas branches), balances with the central bank held to meet the cash reserve requirement plus surplus cash, and balances with banks and money at call and short notice (call money is overnight, notice money 2 to 14 days). Investments are in government securities, other approved securities, shares, debentures and bonds, subsidiaries and joint ventures; banks hold securities partly to comply with SLR. Advances, the most important asset and the major source of income, comprise cash credits, overdrafts and loans repayable on demand, term loans (repayable in instalments), and bills purchased and discounted; classified by security into secured by tangible assets, covered by bank or government guarantees (including DICGC and ECGC cover) and unsecured. Fixed assets are premises, furniture, fixtures, hardware and motor vehicles. Other assets include inter-office adjustments (debit balance), interest accrued, tax paid in advance or deducted at source, stationery and stamps, non-banking assets acquired in satisfaction of claims, and others. Contingent liabilities are obligations under letters of credit, guarantees and acceptances, claims not acknowledged as debts, liabilities on outstanding forward exchange contracts and other items not on the balance sheet.

Profit and loss account (courseware): income is interest income and other income; expenses are interest expended, operating expenses and provisions and contingencies. Interest income, the major revenue, comes from interest and discount on advances and bills, income on investments (interest and dividend), interest on balances with the central bank and other banks and call money placements, and other interest. Other income: commission, exchange and brokerage (collections, letters of credit and guarantees, government business, locker rent, remittance charges), profit or loss on sale and revaluation of investments, profit on sale of land, buildings and other assets, profit on exchange transactions, dividend income from subsidiaries and joint ventures, and miscellaneous income. Interest expended is interest on deposits, on borrowings from the central bank and other banks and other interest. Operating expenses include payments to and provisions for employees, rent, taxes and lighting, printing and stationery, advertisement, depreciation on bank property, directors fees, auditors fees, law charges, postage, repairs, insurance (including premium to the deposit insurance and credit guarantee corporations) and other expenditure. Provisions and contingencies (for bad and doubtful debts, taxation, depreciation in investments) are one of the biggest expenses. Net interest income = interest income less interest expended; operating profit = income less expenditure before provisions; net profit after provisions and taxes.

Meaning of ALM (courseware): the business of banking involves identifying, measuring, accepting and managing risk, so ALM is one of the most important risk-management functions. With deregulation and competition narrowing spreads, administered interest rates gave way to market pricing; the changes in the profile of sources and uses of funds, the industry profile and exposure limits and interest rate structure created a transition in risk profile. ALM is concerned with strategic balance sheet management involving risks caused by changes in interest rates, exchange rates, credit risk and the liquidity position; it moves from partial asset management (credit and non-performing assets) and partial liability management towards an integrated approach where all balance sheet components and maturity mix are seen from the profit angle. ALM is the act of planning, acquiring and directing the flow of funds through an organisation; its ultimate objective is to generate adequate and stable earnings and build equity over time while taking reasonable and measured business risks. It is management of the net interest margin (NIM) so that its level and riskiness fit risk-return objectives, an integrated approach requiring decisions about the types and amounts of financial assets and the mix and volume of financial liabilities. Balance sheet restructuring is actively managing the composition and mix of assets and liabilities in response to objectives, economic conditions and the future interest rate scenario to prevent undesirable imbalance between asset and liability maturities. ALM involves judgement, planning, directing and controlling the flow, mix, cost and yield of consolidated funds; it does not avoid risk but manages risk sustaining profitability.

Significance of ALM (courseware): a financial institution may have enough assets to pay its liabilities, but if 50 per cent of liabilities mature within one year and only 10 per cent of assets mature within the same period it may be temporarily insolvent through a severe liquidity crisis from asset liability mismatch. ALM matches assets and liabilities to minimise liquidity and market risk; it can be done on a per-liability basis by matching a specific asset to each liability. Even if maturities are matched, interest rates can change during the period, affecting net interest income. ALM views the institution as interrelated sets that must be coordinated, the primary goal being control of interest income and expense and the resulting net interest margin on an ongoing basis. Reasons for growing significance: volatility after deregulation (rate fluctuations affect market value, yields and costs of assets and liabilities and NII); product innovation (for example flexi-deposit, with features that affect the risk profile); regulatory environment (the BIS framework and central bank guidelines); embedded options (a depositor may withdraw prematurely forcing the bank to replace funds at a different cost, called refinancing risk, and a borrower may prepay, forcing the bank to redeploy the funds at a different rate, called reinvestment risk); and management recognition that a good franchise and deposit base are not enough without linking the asset and liability sides.

Purpose, parameters and objectives of ALM (courseware): ALM manages volume, mix, maturity, rate sensitivity, quality and liquidity of assets and liabilities to attain a predetermined acceptable risk-reward ratio; it enhances asset quality, quantifies the risk-reward ratio and manages the associated risks, by reviewing the interest rate structure and pricing of assets and liabilities, examining loan and investment portfolios for exchange rate and liquidity risk and credit and contingency risk, and reviewing actual performance against projections and analysing the effect on spreads. The parameters used to stabilise short-term profits, long-term earnings and long-term substance are: net interest income (NII = interest income - interest expenses, whose fluctuations must be minimised), net interest margin (NIM = NII / average total assets; the spread on earning assets; a higher spread means a higher NIM and direct correlation between risk and return) and the economic equity ratio (shareholders funds to total assets, the ratio of owned funds to total funds, which assesses sustenance capacity). Macro objectives: critical business policies, efficient capital allocation and product design with appropriate pricing; micro objectives: profitability through price matching while ensuring liquidity by maturity matching. Price matching maintains spreads by ensuring liabilities are deployed at a rate higher than their cost; a positive gap (assets more than liabilities) benefits from rising rates, a negative gap (liabilities more than assets) benefits from falling rates. Liquidity is ensured by grouping assets and liabilities by maturing profile and assessing the gap to identify future financing needs.

ALM as coordinated balance sheet management (courseware): a two-stage approach. Stage 1, specific balance sheet management functions: asset side (reserve position management, liquidity management, investment or security management, loan management, fixed assets management) and liability side (liability management, reserve position management, long-term management of notes and debentures, capital management). Stage 2, income-expense functions: profit = interest income - interest expense - provision for loan loss + non-interest revenue - non-interest expense - taxes. Banks formulate policies for spread management, loan quality, generating fee income and service charges, control of non-interest operating expenses, tax management and capital adequacy.

payload.title: Structure of a bank balance sheet
payload.core_explanation_md:
Under **section 29 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949** a commercial bank prepares a **balance sheet** and **profit and loss account** at the **last working day** of the year in the **Third Schedule forms**.

| **Sources of funds** | **Applications of funds** |
| --- | --- |
| Capital | **Cash and balances with the central bank** |
| Reserves | **Balances with banks and money at call and short notice** |
| Deposits | **Investments** |
| Borrowings | **Advances** |
| Other liabilities and provisions | **Fixed assets**, **other assets** |

Liabilities and net worth are **sources**; assets are **uses** that earn revenue.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Both sides total the same: every use of funds is financed by a source.

self_check.prompt_text: Which side of the balance sheet shows uses of funds?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The assets side.

payload.title: Components of liabilities
payload.core_explanation_md:
- **Capital:** owners' stake and a **cushion** for depositors; long-term; minimum set by the **capital adequacy ratio**.
- **Reserves and surplus:** **statutory and capital reserves, share premium, revenue reserves, profit and loss balance**.
- **Deposits (main source):** **demand** (current, overdue, call), **savings** and **term** (fixed, short, recurring).
- **Borrowings:** from the **central bank**, **other banks** and institutions such as **IDBI, EXIM Bank, NABARD**.
- **Other liabilities and provisions:** **bills payable** (drafts, TTs, MTs, bankers cheques), **inter-office adjustments (credit)**, **interest accrued but not due**, **tax and other provisions**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Capital absorbs losses before depositors are affected.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the main source of funds for a bank?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Deposits.

payload.title: Components of assets and contingent liabilities
payload.core_explanation_md:
- **Cash and balances with the central bank:** cash in hand and balances kept for **CRR** and surplus.
- **Balances with banks and call/notice money:** call = **overnight**, notice = **2 to 14 days**.
- **Investments:** **government and approved securities**, shares, debentures, bonds, **subsidiaries and joint ventures**; partly held for **SLR**.
- **Advances:** the **largest income earner**: **cash credit, overdraft and demand loans**, **term loans** (repaid in instalments), **bills purchased and discounted**; by security **secured**, **covered by guarantees (government, DICGC, ECGC)** or **unsecured**.
- **Fixed assets** and **other assets** (inter-office debit balance, interest accrued, tax paid in advance, stationery, **non-banking assets acquired in satisfaction of claims**).

**Contingent liabilities** are **off-balance-sheet** obligations: **letters of credit, guarantees, acceptances**, disputed claims, **forward exchange contracts**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Contingent liabilities become real only if the triggering event occurs.

self_check.prompt_text: Name two contingent liabilities.
self_check.expected_takeaway: For example guarantees and letters of credit.

payload.title: The profit and loss account
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Income** = interest income + other income. **Expenses** = interest expended + operating expenses + provisions and contingencies.

- **Interest income:** advances and bills, **investments**, balances with the central bank and other banks.
- **Other income:** **commission, exchange and brokerage**, **profit on sale and revaluation of investments and assets**, **exchange transactions**, **dividends**.
- **Interest expended:** on **deposits** and **borrowings**.
- **Operating expenses:** **staff**, rent and lighting, printing, advertising, **depreciation**, auditors fees, insurance (including premium to the deposit insurance and credit guarantee bodies) and others.
- **Provisions and contingencies:** one of the **largest** expenses (bad debts, tax, investment depreciation).

**NII = interest income - interest expended.** **Operating profit = income - expenses before provisions.** **Net profit = operating profit - provisions and taxes.**
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Provisions often decide whether the year shows a profit.

self_check.prompt_text: How is net interest income computed?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Interest income less interest expended.

payload.title: NII, NIM and profit arithmetic
payload.core_explanation_md:
**NII = interest income - interest expended.**

**NIM = NII / average total assets x 100.**

**Operating profit = (interest income + other income) - (interest expended + operating expenses).**

**Net profit = operating profit - provisions and contingencies** (the courseware shows tax within provisions and contingencies).

Example: interest income **Rs 900 crore**, interest expended **Rs 540 crore**, average assets **Rs 9,000 crore**: NII **Rs 360 crore**; NIM **4.0 per cent**.

variables.name: Average of opening and closing total assets

common_errors: Using total income instead of NII

payload.expanded_explanation_md: NIM is the spread earned per rupee of assets.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the denominator of NIM?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Average total assets.

payload.title: What ALM is
payload.core_explanation_md:
The business of banking is **identifying, measuring, accepting and managing risk**, so **ALM** is a core risk function. As deregulation and competition **narrowed spreads** and replaced administered rates, banks moved from **partial asset management** (credit, NPAs) and **partial liability management** to an **integrated balance sheet** view driven by **profit**.

- **ALM** = **planning, acquiring and directing the flow of funds**; the aim is **adequate, stable earnings** and growth of equity with **reasonable, measured risk**.
- It manages the **net interest margin** so its **level and riskiness** fit the **risk-return objectives**.
- **Balance sheet restructuring** = actively adjusting the **mix** of assets and liabilities to **objectives, economic conditions and the expected rate scenario**.
- ALM **does not avoid risk**; it manages it **while sustaining profit**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: It involves judgement, planning, directing and controlling the cost, yield, mix and flow of funds.

self_check.prompt_text: Does ALM aim to eliminate risk?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No; it manages risk while sustaining profitability.

payload.title: Why ALM has grown in importance
payload.core_explanation_md:
An institution may hold **enough assets overall** yet face a crisis: if **50 per cent of liabilities** fall due within a year but only **10 per cent of assets** mature then, it can be **temporarily insolvent** through **liquidity** failure. ALM matches assets and liabilities (even **per liability**), but interest rates can still change **during** the period, affecting NII.

**Reasons:**

1. **Volatility** after deregulation affects **market values, yields and NII**.
2. **Product innovation** (for example **flexi-deposits**) alters the risk profile.
3. **Regulation:** the **BIS framework** and central bank guidelines.
4. **Embedded options:** early **deposit withdrawal** forces the bank to replace funds at a different cost (**refinancing risk**); **loan prepayment** forces redeployment at a different rate (**reinvestment risk**).
5. **Management recognition:** a good franchise and deposit base are not enough without **linking the asset and liability sides**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Refinancing risk is on the liability side; reinvestment risk is on the asset side.

self_check.prompt_text: What is reinvestment risk?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The risk that after a prepayment the bank must redeploy the funds at a different, perhaps lower, rate.

payload.title: Parameters and objectives of ALM
payload.core_explanation_md:
ALM manages **volume, mix, maturity, rate sensitivity, quality and liquidity** to reach an acceptable **risk-reward ratio**.

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **NII** | **Interest income - interest expenses**: stabilise short-term profit |
| **NIM** | **NII / average total assets**: the **spread on earning assets** |
| **Economic equity ratio** | **Shareholders funds / total assets**: sustenance capacity |

**Objectives:** at the **macro** level: **business policy, capital allocation, product design and pricing**. At the **micro** level: **profitability through price matching** and **liquidity through maturity matching**.

- **Price matching:** keep liabilities deployed at a rate above their cost. **Positive gap** (assets > liabilities) benefits from **rising** rates; **negative gap** from **falling** rates.
- **Liquidity:** group assets and liabilities by maturity and use the **gap** to see future funding needs.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Higher spreads usually come with higher risk; the aim is managed risk, not none.

self_check.prompt_text: Which gap position benefits from rising interest rates?
self_check.expected_takeaway: A positive gap, where assets exceed liabilities in the repricing bucket.

payload.title: ALM as coordinated balance sheet management
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Stage 1: specific balance sheet functions**

- **Assets:** reserve position, liquidity, **investment**, **loan** and **fixed asset** management.
- **Liabilities:** liability management, reserve position, **long-term notes and debentures**, **capital** management.

**Stage 2: income and expense functions**

**Profit = interest income - interest expense - provision for loan loss + non-interest revenue - non-interest expense - taxes.**

Policies are needed for **spread management**, **loan quality**, **fee and service charge income**, **control of non-interest expenses**, **tax management** and **capital adequacy**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Stage 2 links the balance sheet to the profit and loss account.

self_check.prompt_text: Name two stage 2 policy areas.
self_check.expected_takeaway: For example spread management and control of non-interest operating expenses.

payload.title: Profit identity
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Profit = interest income - interest expense - loan loss provision + non-interest revenue - non-interest expense - taxes.**

Example: **1,200 - 700 - 90 + 260 - 400 - 70 = Rs 200 crore**.

payload.expanded_explanation_md: Each term corresponds to a policy lever.

self_check.prompt_text: Which items reduce profit in the identity?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Interest expense, loan loss provision, non-interest expense and taxes.

unresolved: The courseware tables of the consolidated balance sheet and the income and expenditure of scheduled commercial banks at March 2021 (amounts by bank group, NIM by group) are statistical illustrations from a central bank report; they were not checked and are not taught or tested as facts. The statutory forms (Third Schedule of the Banking Regulation Act, section 29) are taught only as the courseware states them.
The courseware explanation of ALM is general; the detailed regulatory ALM guidelines are covered in other units of this module and the earlier Treasury batch.
The courseware definition of the economic equity ratio (owned funds to total funds) is taught as stated; the ratio is not a regulatory measure.
The courseware describes refinancing risk and reinvestment risk through embedded options in a single paragraph; taught as stated.

items.title: Structure of a bank balance sheet
items.core_explanation_md:
Under **section 29 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949** a commercial bank prepares a **balance sheet** and **profit and loss account** at the **last working day** of the year in the **Third Schedule forms**.

| **Sources of funds** | **Applications of funds** |
| --- | --- |
| Capital | **Cash and balances with the central bank** |
| Reserves | **Balances with banks and money at call and short notice** |
| Deposits | **Investments** |
| Borrowings | **Advances** |
| Other liabilities and provisions | **Fixed assets**, **other assets** |

Liabilities and net worth are **sources**; assets are **uses** that earn revenue.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Both sides total the same: every use of funds is financed by a source.

self_check.prompt_text: Which side of the balance sheet shows uses of funds?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The assets side.

items.title: Components of liabilities
items.core_explanation_md:
- **Capital:** owners' stake and a **cushion** for depositors; long-term; minimum set by the **capital adequacy ratio**.
- **Reserves and surplus:** **statutory and capital reserves, share premium, revenue reserves, profit and loss balance**.
- **Deposits (main source):** **demand** (current, overdue, call), **savings** and **term** (fixed, short, recurring).
- **Borrowings:** from the **central bank**, **other banks** and institutions such as **IDBI, EXIM Bank, NABARD**.
- **Other liabilities and provisions:** **bills payable** (drafts, TTs, MTs, bankers cheques), **inter-office adjustments (credit)**, **interest accrued but not due**, **tax and other provisions**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Capital absorbs losses before depositors are affected.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the main source of funds for a bank?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Deposits.

items.title: Components of assets and contingent liabilities
items.core_explanation_md:
- **Cash and balances with the central bank:** cash in hand and balances kept for **CRR** and surplus.
- **Balances with banks and call/notice money:** call = **overnight**, notice = **2 to 14 days**.
- **Investments:** **government and approved securities**, shares, debentures, bonds, **subsidiaries and joint ventures**; partly held for **SLR**.
- **Advances:** the **largest income earner**: **cash credit, overdraft and demand loans**, **term loans** (repaid in instalments), **bills purchased and discounted**; by security **secured**, **covered by guarantees (government, DICGC, ECGC)** or **unsecured**.
- **Fixed assets** and **other assets** (inter-office debit balance, interest accrued, tax paid in advance, stationery, **non-banking assets acquired in satisfaction of claims**).

**Contingent liabilities** are **off-balance-sheet** obligations: **letters of credit, guarantees, acceptances**, disputed claims, **forward exchange contracts**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Contingent liabilities become real only if the triggering event occurs.

self_check.prompt_text: Name two contingent liabilities.
self_check.expected_takeaway: For example guarantees and letters of credit.

items.title: The profit and loss account
items.core_explanation_md:
**Income** = interest income + other income. **Expenses** = interest expended + operating expenses + provisions and contingencies.

- **Interest income:** advances and bills, **investments**, balances with the central bank and other banks.
- **Other income:** **commission, exchange and brokerage**, **profit on sale and revaluation of investments and assets**, **exchange transactions**, **dividends**.
- **Interest expended:** on **deposits** and **borrowings**.
- **Operating expenses:** **staff**, rent and lighting, printing, advertising, **depreciation**, auditors fees, insurance (including premium to the deposit insurance and credit guarantee bodies) and others.
- **Provisions and contingencies:** one of the **largest** expenses (bad debts, tax, investment depreciation).

**NII = interest income - interest expended.** **Operating profit = income - expenses before provisions.** **Net profit = operating profit - provisions and taxes.**
items.expanded_explanation_md: Provisions often decide whether the year shows a profit.

self_check.prompt_text: How is net interest income computed?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Interest income less interest expended.

items.title: NII, NIM and profit arithmetic
items.core_explanation_md:
**NII = interest income - interest expended.**

**NIM = NII / average total assets x 100.**

**Operating profit = (interest income + other income) - (interest expended + operating expenses).**

**Net profit = operating profit - provisions and contingencies** (the courseware shows tax within provisions and contingencies).

Example: interest income **Rs 900 crore**, interest expended **Rs 540 crore**, average assets **Rs 9,000 crore**: NII **Rs 360 crore**; NIM **4.0 per cent**.

common_errors: Using total income instead of NII

items.expanded_explanation_md: NIM is the spread earned per rupee of assets.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the denominator of NIM?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Average total assets.

items.title: What ALM is
items.core_explanation_md:
The business of banking is **identifying, measuring, accepting and managing risk**, so **ALM** is a core risk function. As deregulation and competition **narrowed spreads** and replaced administered rates, banks moved from **partial asset management** (credit, NPAs) and **partial liability management** to an **integrated balance sheet** view driven by **profit**.

- **ALM** = **planning, acquiring and directing the flow of funds**; the aim is **adequate, stable earnings** and growth of equity with **reasonable, measured risk**.
- It manages the **net interest margin** so its **level and riskiness** fit the **risk-return objectives**.
- **Balance sheet restructuring** = actively adjusting the **mix** of assets and liabilities to **objectives, economic conditions and the expected rate scenario**.
- ALM **does not avoid risk**; it manages it **while sustaining profit**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: It involves judgement, planning, directing and controlling the cost, yield, mix and flow of funds.

self_check.prompt_text: Does ALM aim to eliminate risk?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No; it manages risk while sustaining profitability.

items.title: Why ALM has grown in importance
items.core_explanation_md:
An institution may hold **enough assets overall** yet face a crisis: if **50 per cent of liabilities** fall due within a year but only **10 per cent of assets** mature then, it can be **temporarily insolvent** through **liquidity** failure. ALM matches assets and liabilities (even **per liability**), but interest rates can still change **during** the period, affecting NII.

**Reasons:**

1. **Volatility** after deregulation affects **market values, yields and NII**.
2. **Product innovation** (for example **flexi-deposits**) alters the risk profile.
3. **Regulation:** the **BIS framework** and central bank guidelines.
4. **Embedded options:** early **deposit withdrawal** forces the bank to replace funds at a different cost (**refinancing risk**); **loan prepayment** forces redeployment at a different rate (**reinvestment risk**).
5. **Management recognition:** a good franchise and deposit base are not enough without **linking the asset and liability sides**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Refinancing risk is on the liability side; reinvestment risk is on the asset side.

self_check.prompt_text: What is reinvestment risk?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The risk that after a prepayment the bank must redeploy the funds at a different, perhaps lower, rate.

items.title: Parameters and objectives of ALM
items.core_explanation_md:
ALM manages **volume, mix, maturity, rate sensitivity, quality and liquidity** to reach an acceptable **risk-reward ratio**.

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **NII** | **Interest income - interest expenses**: stabilise short-term profit |
| **NIM** | **NII / average total assets**: the **spread on earning assets** |
| **Economic equity ratio** | **Shareholders funds / total assets**: sustenance capacity |

**Objectives:** at the **macro** level: **business policy, capital allocation, product design and pricing**. At the **micro** level: **profitability through price matching** and **liquidity through maturity matching**.

- **Price matching:** keep liabilities deployed at a rate above their cost. **Positive gap** (assets > liabilities) benefits from **rising** rates; **negative gap** from **falling** rates.
- **Liquidity:** group assets and liabilities by maturity and use the **gap** to see future funding needs.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Higher spreads usually come with higher risk; the aim is managed risk, not none.

self_check.prompt_text: Which gap position benefits from rising interest rates?
self_check.expected_takeaway: A positive gap, where assets exceed liabilities in the repricing bucket.

items.title: ALM as coordinated balance sheet management
items.core_explanation_md:
**Stage 1: specific balance sheet functions**

- **Assets:** reserve position, liquidity, **investment**, **loan** and **fixed asset** management.
- **Liabilities:** liability management, reserve position, **long-term notes and debentures**, **capital** management.

**Stage 2: income and expense functions**

**Profit = interest income - interest expense - provision for loan loss + non-interest revenue - non-interest expense - taxes.**

Policies are needed for **spread management**, **loan quality**, **fee and service charge income**, **control of non-interest expenses**, **tax management** and **capital adequacy**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Stage 2 links the balance sheet to the profit and loss account.

self_check.prompt_text: Name two stage 2 policy areas.
self_check.expected_takeaway: For example spread management and control of non-interest operating expenses.

items.title: Profit identity
items.core_explanation_md:
**Profit = interest income - interest expense - loan loss provision + non-interest revenue - non-interest expense - taxes.**

Example: **1,200 - 700 - 90 + 260 - 400 - 70 = Rs 200 crore**.
